'''Stefano Profumo''' (born 25 January 1978) is an Italian-American theoretical physicist and professor at the University of California, Santa Cruz. He works on particle dark matter, high-energy astrophysics, and black hole physics.<ref name="profumo-ucsc">{{cite web
 | title = Stefano Profumo – Faculty Page
 | publisher = Santa Cruz Institute for Particle Physics (SCIPP)
 | url = https://scipp.ucsc.edu/~profumo/
 | access-date = September 23, 2026
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260705044117/https://scipp-legacy.pbsci.ucsc.edu/~profumo/|archive-date=July 5, 2026|url-status=dead}}</ref>  He is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2020/09/aps-fellows/|title=Two UCSC physicists elected Fellows of the American Physical Society|first=Tim|last=Stephens|date=September 29, 2020}}</ref> and a recipient of the 2009 Department of Energy's Outstanding Junior Investigator Award.<ref name="profumo-ucsc" />

== Early life and education ==
Profumo studied physics at the [[University of Pisa]] (B.Sc., 2001)<ref name="profumo-ucsc" /> and theoretical physics at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]] (M.Sc., 2001).<ref name="profumo-ucsc" /> He earned a Ph.D. in elementary particle theory at the [[International School for Advanced Studies|SISSA–ISAS]] in Trieste, Italy, in 2004.<ref name="profumo-ucsc" /> He subsequently held postdoctoral appointments at [[Florida State University]] (2004–2005) and the [[California Institute of Technology]] (2005–2007).<ref name="inspire-profumo">{{cite web
 | title = Stefano Profumo – Author Profile
 | url = https://inspirehep.net/authors/1019758
 | publisher = InspireHEP
 | access-date = 2025-10-06
}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Profumo joined the faculty of the Department of Physics at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]] in 2007 as an assistant professor. He became associate professor with tenure in 2011 and full professor in 2015.<ref name="inspire-profumo" />  Since 2015 he has served as director of graduate studies in the physics department, and in 2024 he was appointed Associate Dean for Graduate Studies and Postdoctoral Affairs in the Physical and Biological Sciences Division.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Campus Directory - UC Santa Cruz |url=https://campusdirectory.ucsc.edu/cd_detail?uid=profumo |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=campusdirectory.ucsc.edu}}</ref> He has also been serving as Deputy Director for Theory at the [[Santa Cruz Institute for Particle Physics]] since 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scipp.science.ucsc.edu/|title=Santa Cruz Institute for Particle Physics – The cutting edge of experimental & theoretical particle physics|website=scipp.science.ucsc.edu}}</ref>

Profumo's research covers particle physics beyond the Standard Model, models of baryogenesis, and astro-particle physics including dark matter searches, high-energy astrophysical phenomena, and black hole physics.<ref name="profumo-ucsc" /><ref name="inspire-profumo" /> His work has been often featured in the popular press.

== Publications ==
Profumo is the co-author of the invited review "Dark Matter" in the ''Review of Particle Physics'' (with Laura Baudis, 2020–present).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Particle Data Group |url=https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/contents_sports.html |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=}}</ref> His textbook ''An Introduction to Particle Dark Matter'' was published by World Scientific in 2017.<ref>{{Cite book |title=An Introduction to Particle Dark Matter {{!}} Advanced Textbooks in Physics |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/q0001 |access-date=2025-10-04  |date=2017 |language=en |doi=10.1142/q0001 |isbn=978-1-78634-000-9 }}</ref> He is also the author of ''Advanced Physics Problems and Solutions, Volume 1: Classical Mechanics and Mathematical Methods'',<ref name="appsv1">{{Cite book
 | last = Profumo
 | first = Stefano
 | title = Advanced Physics Problems and Solutions – Volume 1: Classical Mechanics and Mathematical Methods
 | series = Advanced Textbooks in Physics
 | publisher = World Scientific
 | url = https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/q0555
 | doi = 10.1142/q0555
 | issn = 2059-7711
}}</ref> and ''Advanced Physics Problems and Solutions, Volume 2: Electricity and Magnetism, Quantum Mechanics, and Statistical Mechanics'',<ref name="appsv2">{{Cite book
 | last = Profumo
 | first = Stefano
 | title = Advanced Physics Problems and Solutions – Volume 2: Electricity and Magnetism, Quantum Mechanics, and Statistical Mechanics
 | series = Advanced Textbooks in Physics
 | publisher = World Scientific
 | url = https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/q0556
 | doi = 10.1142/q0556
 | isbn = 978-1-80061-894-7
 | issn = 2059-7711
}}</ref> both published by World Scientific in the ''Advanced Textbooks in Physics'' series.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Advanced Textbooks in Physics |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/series/atip |publisher=World Scientific |access-date=2025-10-06}}</ref> As of 2025, his work has been cited more than 42,000 times, with an h-index of 83, according to Google Scholar.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=4I8EuFkAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Stefano Profumo|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

== Professional service ==
He was a founding editor and is the Editor-in-Chief of ''Physics of the Dark Universe'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics of the Dark Universe {{!}} Journal {{!}} ScienceDirect.com by Elsevier |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/physics-of-the-dark-universe |access-date=2025-10-04 |website=www.sciencedirect.com |language=en-us}}</ref> he is Editor-in-Chief of ''Astrophysical Frontiers'',<ref>{{cite web
 | title = Editorial board - Astrophysical Frontiers (ApF)
 | publisher = SCILTP (Scilight)
 | url = https://www.sciltp.com/journals/apf/editorial-board
 | access-date = 2025-10-06
}}</ref> he is on the editorial board of ''Asymmetry''<ref>{{cite web
 | title = Editorial Board - Asymmetry
 | publisher = ELS Publication (or Asymmetry journal)
 | url = https://www.elspub.com/journals/asymmetry/editorial/
 | access-date = 2025-10-06
}}</ref> and of ''Particles'' in the ''Phenomenology and Physics Beyond the Standard Model'' section,<ref>{{cite web
 | title = Editorial Board — Phenomenology and Physics Beyond the Standard Model (Particles, MDPI)
 | publisher = MDPI
 | url = https://www.mdpi.com/journal/particles/sectioneditors/phenomenology_physics_standard_model
 | access-date = 2025-10-06
}}</ref> he is a section board member in the ''Particles'' journal (Astroparticle Physics & Cosmology section)<ref>{{cite web
 | title = Astroparticle Physics and Cosmology Section — Particles (MDPI)
 | publisher = MDPI
 | url = https://www.mdpi.com/journal/particles/sectioneditors/astroparticle_physics_cosmology
 | access-date = 2025-10-06
}}</ref>; He also serves on the editorial board of Physical Review Letters.
